Wagh said the offer was revised earlier this month to compensate shareholders for a four-month delay in securing regulatory approvals across multiple countries. The company raised its bid to â‚¬14.40 per share on October 9 from â‚¬14.10, describing the revised price as its best and final offer. Asked whether the demand of minority shareholders could jeopardise the transaction, Wagh said Tata Motors remained confident following the approval of all resolutions at Iveco's extraordinary general meeting (EGM) earlier this month.

title: Co Rules out Further Increase in Iveco Offer
